VibePascal v56 Win64 compiler -- an inferred inline var initialised from a real
constant is a Double, whatever the constant's value happens to be
Source commit: a187bbac34e1f61154affa5a57e93298028ffc72
Compiler fix:  f06e46d8eb  (compiler/pstatmnt.pas, compiler/defutil.pas, compiler/ncnv.pas)
Parent release: v55 (eae5d3e919a26a7db19937da10da1c8b610b17da)
Built: 2026-09-10, cross-compiled Linux x86_64 -> Win64 (-Apecoff -Xi) from the
       self-hosted Linux compiler e6de1f00eccb9b5ccf028bee7e7342ad
ppcx64.exe md5:    13153B27FF17306EEA63CFAD0FC17AB5
ppcx64.exe sha256: 6732D995A163213E1CD080644C3F660430E1BC34EF265BF2812A862B59DB9656

WHAT WAS BROKEN
---------------
An inline var with no type annotation took its type from the real constant you
initialised it with -- and that type changes with the VALUE:

    var a := 1.0;      // Single   -  4 bytes,  7 digits
    var b := 0.1;      // Extended - 10 bytes, 19 digits
    var c := 1.0/3.0;  // Single, or Extended under {$mode delphi}
    var d := 1/2;      // Double

Four declarations side by side, four different types, and none of them the one
you get from Delphi or from writing `var x: Double := ...` yourself.  The
4-byte case is the one that bites: `var pi := 3.14159265358979` kept about
seven digits, silently, and the same variable widened to fifteen the moment
somebody edited the literal to one a Single cannot represent exactly.

Lars hit the other end of it in the Lazarus IDE: code completion said one type,
the compiler used another.

WHAT CHANGED
------------
An un-annotated inline var initialised from a real CONSTANT now infers the
default real type -- Double.  It is the third rule of the same family as v54's
`var i := -1` -> NativeInt and `var s := 'x'` -> the default string type:
inference gives you the DEFAULT type of a kind, not the narrowest one that
happens to fit today's literal.

Double rather than Extended because Extended is an x87-only 80-bit type, and
Delphi makes Extended an alias of Double on every 64-bit target we ship.

What deliberately does NOT change:

  * RANGE is never lost.  1.0e400 and 1.0e-4000 keep the wider type they were
    given -- a Double would silently hold +Inf and 0.  Precision digits can be
    lost, because that is what asking for a Double means.
  * A VARIABLE or a non-constant expression keeps its own type, exactly as
    Delphi infers it.  `var m := someSingle` is still a Single.
  * An explicit typecast still wins: `var j := single(1.0)` is a Single.
    (Making that true was part of this fix -- see below.)
  * Currency and Comp are untouched.
  * `var d := 1/2` was already a Double and stays one.
  * How real CONSTANTS themselves are typed is NOT touched.  That is stock FPC
    behaviour driven by $MINFPCONSTPREC (default s32real) and $EXCESSPRECISION
    (on in delphi mode), both byte-identical to upstream here, and both still
    available to anyone who wants to ask for something else explicitly.

One supporting change with a wider reach, and worth knowing about: a typecast
to the type a real constant ALREADY has -- single(1.0), extended(0.1) -- was
dropped by the compiler without recording that the user had asked for it, so
the surviving constant was indistinguishable from a bare literal.  It now
carries that mark, the way the same constant already did when the cast changed
its type.  Nothing else in the compiler reads that mark on a constant, and the
full test corpus is unchanged by it.

VALIDATION
----------
Verified on isolated throwaway A/B compilers, real toolchain untouched.  The
baseline built that way came out byte-identical to the shipped v55 Linux
compiler (19f526bd6be0ec63fca96c4d1b77e19d), which is what makes the A/B
trustworthy rather than merely tidy.

  * tinlinevarrealinfer1.pp -- 57 checks over 10 structural contexts (free
    procedure, method, nested block, nested procedure, with-block, for-loop
    body, except and finally blocks, while/repeat/case, closure capture, main
    program body), crossed with the compiler MODE, because delphi mode changes
    how a constant fold is widened:
        -Munleashed        baseline 37 failures -> 0 of 57
        -Mdelphi           baseline 36 failures -> 0 of 54
        -Mdelphiunicode    baseline 36 failures -> 0 of 54
    Sizes AND values are checked: an inferred variable has to hold exactly what
    the explicitly declared one holds, including when a closure captures it.
  * tinlinevarrealinfer2.pp -- a must-FAIL test.  `for var i := 1.0 to 2.0` is
    still rejected, cleanly, with no internal error.
  * Full tests/test corpus, 1982 tests: 1981 SAME, 0 DIFF, after a
    baseline-against-baseline control run that was also 0 DIFF.
  * Self-host fixpoint: stage2 == stage3, byte-identical
    (e6de1f00eccb9b5ccf028bee7e7342ad).
  * The neighbouring inference rules are unmoved: tinlinevarnativeint1 45/45
    and tinlinevarstrinfer1 20/20, both under -Munleashed and -Mdelphiunicode.

UNITS
-----
Compiler binary only.  No PPU format, RTL or package change, so the v52 unit
set stays valid -- an existing v52/v53/v54/v55 install can take this ~3.5 MB
bin tarball on its own.

Windows runtime evidence for these exact bytes is recorded in dist/win64/LATEST.txt.
Nobody has yet run any VibePascal release on real Windows hardware; the runtime
proof here is wine, which is not Windows.
